meta.title: AI Workload Control Mapper
meta.note: Provider-neutral control objectives for AI workloads, each mapped to the closest native service on AWS, Azure and Google Cloud. Guidance to adapt, not an audit, and not a substitute for provider documentation. Cloud services are renamed and reshuffled often: treat the objective as durable and verify the service name before you put it in a client deliverable.

tiers.name: AI that answers
tiers.hint: A model generates responses. No access to your data, no ability to act.
tiers.example: A support assistant answering from the model's own training, a drafting or summarizing helper.

tiers.name: AI that connects
tiers.hint: The model reaches your enterprise data, usually through retrieval (RAG).
tiers.example: A policy assistant grounded in your intranet, a search layer over contracts or tickets.

tiers.name: AI that acts
tiers.hint: An agent takes actions: calling tools, writing to systems, executing code, transacting.
tiers.example: An agent that files tickets, updates records, moves money, or runs remediation.

layers.name: Infrastructure
layers.hint: Isolation, network paths, and the compute the model runs on.

layers.name: Identity and data
layers.hint: Who and what may reach the model, and what happens to the data.

layers.name: AI application
layers.hint: Filtering, monitoring and behavior at the model and agent boundary.

phases.name: Foundational
phases.hint: Zero to prototype. Extend the controls you already have and get identity right on day one.

phases.name: Enhanced
phases.hint: Prototype to production. Add threat detection, classification and real monitoring.

phases.name: Advanced
phases.hint: Continuous improvement. Automate governance and evidence at scale.

controls.objective: Keep model traffic on a private network path instead of the public internet
controls.rationale: A model endpoint reachable from the internet is a credential-guessing target and puts your prompts, which routinely contain business-sensitive text, on a path you do not control.

services.aws: VPC endpoints (AWS PrivateLink) to Amazon Bedrock
services.azure: Private endpoints and Azure Private Link for Microsoft Foundry and Azure OpenAI
services.gcp: VPC Service Controls perimeter around Vertex AI, plus Private Service Connect

controls.objective: Run inference on isolated compute where the workload is attested and memory is protected
controls.rationale: For regulated or high-sensitivity data, the question is not only who can call the model but who could read the data while it is being processed.

services.aws: AWS Nitro System, Nitro Enclaves for the most sensitive workloads
services.azure: Azure confidential computing (confidential VMs and containers)
services.gcp: Confidential Computing (Confidential VMs)

controls.objective: Explicitly authorize which principals may invoke which models
controls.rationale: Model access defaults are the new S3 bucket permissions. If any principal in the account can call any model, you have no ability to say who used what, and no way to contain misuse.

services.aws: IAM identity-based policies scoped per model on Bedrock InvokeModel
services.azure: Microsoft Entra ID with Azure RBAC on the Foundry or Azure OpenAI resource
services.gcp: Cloud IAM roles on Vertex AI, scoped per model and per service account

controls.objective: Hold your own encryption keys for prompts, outputs and tuning data
controls.rationale: Customer-managed keys give you a revocation lever and an audit trail that provider-managed keys do not. For regulated data this is usually the difference between an approved and a blocked use case.

services.aws: AWS KMS customer managed keys
services.azure: Customer-managed keys backed by Azure Key Vault
services.gcp: CMEK via Cloud KMS

controls.objective: Log every model invocation so you can reconstruct what was asked and what was answered
controls.rationale: Without invocation logging you cannot investigate a data leak, prove a model did not say something, or answer a regulator. Control plane logs alone tell you who configured the model, not who used it.

services.aws: Bedrock model invocation logging for the data plane, AWS CloudTrail for the control plane
services.azure: Azure Monitor diagnostic settings on the Foundry resource, plus Microsoft Purview Audit
services.gcp: Cloud Logging for request and response logging, plus Cloud Audit Logs

controls.objective: Cap spend and request rate, and treat an anomalous spike as a security event
controls.rationale: Stolen model credentials are now resold as inference capacity. Unbounded consumption shows up on the bill before it shows up in the SIEM, so the budget alert is a detection control.

services.aws: Service quotas and AWS Budgets, with GuardDuty AI Protection for cost-harvesting detection
services.azure: Tokens-per-minute quotas on the deployment, plus Cost Management alerts
services.gcp: Vertex AI quotas and Cloud Billing budget alerts

controls.objective: Filter model input and output for harmful content, denied topics and sensitive data
controls.rationale: The model will produce whatever the training data and the prompt lead it to. Filtering at the boundary is the only control that sits between the model and the user.

services.aws: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails (content filters, denied topics, sensitive information filters)
services.azure: Azure AI Content Safety content filters in Microsoft Foundry
services.gcp: Model Armor Input Shield and Output Shield, with Sensitive Data Protection

controls.objective: Defend against prompt injection and jailbreak attempts at the boundary
controls.rationale: Prompt injection is the top item on the OWASP list for a reason: it is the one attack with no clean architectural fix, because instructions and data arrive on the same channel. Boundary defenses reduce it; nothing eliminates it.

services.aws: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails
services.azure: Azure AI Content Safety Prompt Shields
services.gcp: Model Armor Input Shield (jailbreak and prompt injection detection)

controls.objective: Check outputs for groundedness before a user sees them
controls.rationale: A confident wrong answer is a business risk, not a quality nit, once the output feeds a decision. Groundedness checking catches the class of failure that content filters miss entirely.

services.aws: Bedrock Guardrails contextual grounding checks
services.azure: Azure AI Content Safety groundedness detection
services.gcp: Vertex AI grounding with Model Armor output inspection

controls.objective: Detect AI-specific runtime threats, not just infrastructure threats
controls.rationale: Your existing detection stack does not know what an anomalous model invocation looks like. AI threat detection is a separate signal set: unusual invocation patterns, injection attempts, and abuse of inference capacity.

services.aws: Amazon GuardDuty AI Protection, with GuardDuty Extended Threat Detection
services.azure: Microsoft Defender for Cloud threat protection for AI services
services.gcp: AI Protection in Security Command Center

controls.objective: Keep a live inventory of every model, endpoint and agent in use
controls.rationale: You cannot govern what you cannot enumerate, and AI assets appear faster than change control catches them. The inventory is the precondition for every other control on this list.

services.aws: Security Hub AI inventory (Bedrock models, SageMaker endpoints, AgentCore agents)
services.azure: Microsoft Defender for Cloud AI security posture, with Purview DSPM for AI
services.gcp: AI Protection in Security Command Center

controls.objective: Detect AI use that never came through your intake process
controls.rationale: The governed use cases are not the risk. The ungoverned ones are, and they are usually in a browser tab or an unmanaged SaaS integration rather than in your cloud account.

services.aws: Network and CASB telemetry outside the AI stack, plus Security Hub inventory drift
services.azure: Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps discovery, with Purview DSPM for AI
services.gcp: Security Command Center posture findings with Chrome Enterprise and proxy telemetry

controls.objective: Classify and label data before it reaches the index, not after
controls.rationale: Once sensitive content is embedded and indexed it is effectively unlabelled and hard to retract. Classification has to be a gate on ingestion, which is the single most common thing teams get backwards.

services.aws: Amazon Macie for discovery and classification, with Lake Formation on the source data
services.azure: Microsoft Purview information protection and sensitivity labels
services.gcp: Sensitive Data Protection, including automated discovery over Vertex AI datasets

controls.objective: Make retrieval inherit the asking user's entitlements, never the application's
controls.rationale: This is the failure that turns a helpful assistant into an exfiltration path. If the retrieval layer queries with broad service credentials, every user effectively reads everything the index can see, and it bypasses every access control the business believes it has.

services.aws: Per-user session policies and metadata filtering at query time in the knowledge base
services.azure: Entra ID identity passthrough with security trimming, governed by Purview data security policies
services.gcp: Per-user IAM with document-level ACL filtering in Vertex AI Search

controls.objective: Isolate tenants and sensitive corpora in the vector store
controls.rationale: Embeddings from different tenants sharing one index is a data-boundary decision disguised as an architecture choice, and similarity search does not respect logical separation by itself.

services.aws: Separate knowledge bases or namespaces, with IAM and metadata filters per tenant
services.azure: Separate indexes or security filters in Azure AI Search
services.gcp: Separate Vertex AI Search data stores or namespace partitioning

controls.objective: Govern the source data plane the index is built from
controls.rationale: The index inherits every permissions mistake in the source. Fixing retrieval without fixing the lake underneath it just moves the problem one layer down.

services.aws: AWS Lake Formation permissions on the source data
services.azure: Microsoft Purview data governance over the source estate
services.gcp: Dataplex governance with BigQuery and Cloud Storage IAM

controls.objective: Track provenance and freshness of indexed content
controls.rationale: Two different failures share one fix. Poisoned content injects instructions the model will follow, and stale content produces answers that were true last quarter. Both are answered by knowing where each chunk came from and when.

services.aws: Ingestion pipeline metadata with S3 object versioning and re-index scheduling
services.azure: Indexer schedules and source metadata in Azure AI Search
services.gcp: Data store refresh scheduling with source metadata in Vertex AI Search

controls.objective: Redact sensitive values from prompts and responses in flight
controls.rationale: Classification stops the wrong document being indexed. Redaction stops the right document leaking the wrong field, which is the residual risk once retrieval is working correctly.

services.aws: Bedrock Guardrails sensitive information filters
services.azure: Azure AI Content Safety with Purview data loss prevention
services.gcp: Model Armor with Sensitive Data Protection de-identification

controls.objective: Log which documents were retrieved, not only the prompt and response
controls.rationale: When someone asks what the assistant exposed, the prompt log cannot answer it. The retrieval log is the evidence, and it is the artifact an incident responder and an auditor both want.

services.aws: Knowledge base retrieval logging alongside Bedrock invocation logs
services.azure: Azure AI Search diagnostic logs correlated with Foundry telemetry
services.gcp: Vertex AI Search query logging in Cloud Logging

controls.objective: Keep the vector store and its source data inside the same network perimeter as the model
controls.rationale: A private path to the model means little if the retrieval layer reaches across the public internet to fetch the data. The perimeter has to cover the whole call chain.

services.aws: VPC endpoints for the knowledge base, vector store and S3 sources
services.azure: Private endpoints across Azure AI Search, Storage and the Foundry resource
services.gcp: VPC Service Controls perimeter covering Vertex AI, Cloud Storage and BigQuery

controls.objective: Give every agent its own distinct identity
controls.rationale: If an agent acts using a shared service account, you cannot answer who did it, and non-repudiation collapses. Distinct agent identity is the precondition for every audit and incident story at this tier.

services.aws: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity
services.azure: Microsoft Entra Agent ID
services.gcp: A dedicated service account per agent, managed through Cloud IAM

controls.objective: Decide explicitly whether the agent acts autonomously or on behalf of a user
controls.rationale: These are different risk models and the choice is usually made implicitly by a developer. An agent holding its own standing credentials while appearing to act for a user is a confused deputy, and it is privilege escalation by design rather than by bug.

services.aws: AgentCore Identity outbound authentication, on-behalf-of or autonomous, via OAuth or API keys
services.azure: Entra Agent ID with on-behalf-of flows for user-delegated actions
services.gcp: Service account impersonation versus end-user credentials, decided per action

controls.objective: Scope each agent to the minimum tool set and data it needs
controls.rationale: Excessive agency is the OWASP failure mode here. Agents accumulate permissions because it is easier to grant broadly once than to scope per task, and the blast radius grows quietly.

services.aws: Least-privilege IAM roles per agent, reviewed with IAM Access Analyzer
services.azure: Azure RBAC per agent identity, reviewed with Entra access reviews
services.gcp: Per-agent IAM roles reviewed with Policy Analyzer and Recommender

controls.objective: Classify and set retention on agent memory
controls.rationale: Agent memory is a data store that nobody classified. It accumulates enterprise content, persists across sessions, and is almost never covered by a retention schedule or a deletion request process.

services.aws: AgentCore Memory, including the self-managed strategy for extraction and consolidation
services.azure: Agent thread and state storage governed under Purview
services.gcp: Agent session and state storage with defined retention in the backing store

controls.objective: Route every tool call through one authorization choke point
controls.rationale: Tools are the agent's hands. If each integration authorizes itself, there is no place to enforce policy, no single log, and no way to revoke a capability across every agent at once.

services.aws: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway, with IAM authorization and MCP support
services.azure: Microsoft Foundry Agent Service tool and connector governance
services.gcp: Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform tool configuration with Model Armor inspection

controls.objective: Maintain a tool inventory and treat it as attack surface
controls.rationale: Every tool an agent can reach is an action it can take, which makes the tool catalogue the agentic equivalent of an asset inventory. Tool descriptions are also an injection surface, since the agent reads them as instructions.

services.aws: AgentCore Gateway target inventory reviewed against Security Hub AI inventory
services.azure: Foundry connector and tool inventory with Defender for Cloud posture findings
services.gcp: Agent tool registry reviewed in Security Command Center AI Protection

controls.objective: Require a human approval gate on high-consequence actions
controls.rationale: This is use case risk tiering applied to actions rather than applications. Low-consequence and reversible actions run autonomously; irreversible, financial or rights-affecting ones stop for a human. Deciding this per action is the whole governance model.

services.aws: Approval step in the agent workflow, enforced outside the model in the calling application
services.azure: Human-in-the-loop approval in the agent workflow or Logic Apps orchestration
services.gcp: Approval step enforced in the orchestrating application, outside the agent

controls.objective: Sandbox code execution and browsing away from production
controls.rationale: An agent that can run code or browse is executing untrusted, model-generated instructions. That belongs in an isolated runtime with no standing credentials to anything that matters.

services.aws: AgentCore Code Interpreter and AgentCore Browser
services.azure: Microsoft Foundry sandboxed code interpreter
services.gcp: Sandboxed code execution in the agent runtime, isolated from production projects

controls.objective: Bound the blast radius of any single agent run
controls.rationale: Autonomy plus a loop is how a small error becomes a large one. Rate limits, transaction caps and a defined reversal path turn an incident into an inconvenience.

services.aws: Rate and concurrency limits on the agent runtime, with per-action transaction caps in the tool layer
services.azure: Throughput limits on the agent deployment with caps enforced in the connector layer
services.gcp: Quotas on the agent platform with caps enforced in the tool implementation

controls.objective: Treat end-to-end agent traces as audit evidence, not just ops telemetry
controls.rationale: When a regulator or a customer asks what the agent did and why, the answer is a trace: the prompt, the tools called, the arguments, the results, the decision. If that is sampled or short-retention, you cannot answer.

services.aws: AgentCore Observability, CloudWatch-backed and OTEL compatible
services.azure: Azure Monitor and Application Insights tracing on the agent service
services.gcp: Cloud Trace and Cloud Logging across the agent execution path

controls.objective: Detect agentic threats specifically, including tool poisoning and chained abuse
controls.rationale: Agentic attacks look legitimate at every individual step. The signal is in the sequence, which means detection has to understand agent behavior rather than only API calls.

services.aws: GuardDuty AI Protection with AI-powered investigations and MITRE ATT&CK mapping
services.azure: Microsoft Defender for Cloud AI threat protection with Foundry runtime alerts
services.gcp: AI Protection in Security Command Center, agentic threat detection with Model Armor

controls.objective: Isolate the agent runtime from systems it has no business reaching
controls.rationale: Network reachability is a permission you did not write down. An agent runtime sitting in a flat production network can reach far more than its IAM policy suggests.

services.aws: Dedicated VPC and security groups for the agent runtime, egress controlled
services.azure: Network isolation for the agent service with private endpoints and egress control
services.gcp: Dedicated project and VPC Service Controls perimeter for the agent runtime

controls.objective: Be able to stop every agent quickly, and know who can do it
controls.rationale: The question is not whether an agent will misbehave, it is how long it runs before someone stops it. A tested stop path with a named owner is the difference between minutes and a weekend.

services.aws: Disable the agent identity and revoke gateway targets, rehearsed as a runbook
services.azure: Disable the Entra Agent ID and the agent deployment, rehearsed as a runbook
services.gcp: Disable the agent service account and platform deployment, rehearsed as a runbook
